written.myAnswer: Qualitative data describes qualities or categories, while quantitative data represents quantities using numbers.
A student's height is continuous data because it is measured and can take fractional or decimal values within a range.
The number of students in a class is discrete data because it is countable and takes separate whole-number values.
Discrete data is useful for counting separate items, such as recording the whole-number count of students present in class each day.
Qualitative data describes qualities or categories, such as colours or types of fruit. Quantitative data consists of numerical measurements or counts, such as height, weight, or test scores.

Discrete data takes distinct, countable values, such as the number of students attending class. Continuous data can take any value within a range, including fractions or decimals, such as students' heights or the time taken to complete a test.

Nominal data consists of unordered categories, such as favourite colours; a bar chart can display their frequencies. Ordinal data consists of ordered categories, such as satisfaction ratings; an ordered bar chart can display response counts. Discrete data consists of countable values, such as the number of students absent each day; a bar chart can compare the counts. Continuous data can take any value within a range, such as students' heights; a histogram can show its distribution.
